caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the handy_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

This is static build/package evidence only. ARM64 is build-identity-bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. ARMHF's maximum GLIBCXX_3.4 is within the observed Miyoo Mini fallback provider ceiling GLIBCXX_3.4.24, so both the Mini and A30 profiles clear the ABI screen. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every execution profile and device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The fresh core-named publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent local-profile build-core run reproduced both ABI artifacts, metadata, build logs, and the package byte for byte; both runs satisfied the exact mixed-language compile and link proof.

The build command scopes exact native leading-space version ' bc55d46' through C++ GIT_VERSION only; the fail-closed proof binds 13 C and 12 C++ compiles per ABI, exact output/source/argv sets, and the final link-object set. Both ABI logs are warning-free, and the binary reports Handy 0.97.

The resolver info advertises version 0.95 while the built core reports 0.97, so presentation metadata remains a target-integration gate rather than a reason to rewrite upstream metadata during the build.

The resolver Zlib label omits linked LGPL-2.1-or-later, GPL-2.0-or-later, and permissive notices in the compiled source; any public distribution or release remains a human legal/policy and corresponding-source gate.
Atari Lynx content loading, controls, rotation, audio/video pacing, saves, states, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates; static build evidence does not establish device eligibility.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and is bound to ra64-universal-v1; ARMHF reaches GLIBC_2.7 and is bound only to ra32-a30-v1. Handy may be a ra32-universal-v0 candidate only after provider and target-runtime capture; no device view is currently eligible.
